Not among the nine dated owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md §3, and not a brand/gateway/subscription product difference — hook payload key names are neither renamed nor dropped by the de-brand. correctedState: Confirmed, with a severity correction: the value is present, the key is wrong. The sole producer is packages/pi-agent-server/src/extensions/lifecycle-bridge.ts:168-172, which on a `user_bash` cwd delta emits `{hook_event_name:'CwdChanged', cwd, previous_cwd?}`; automations/types.ts:801-802 and the frozen contract row at types.ts:72 declare the same two keys. Our common `cwd` already carries the NEW directory, which is exactly what the doc's own example puts in `cwd` ("/Users/my-project/src" == `new_cwd`), so `new_cwd` is a missing ALIAS rather than missing data; the old directory is carried, but under the non-contract key `previous_cwd` instead of `old_cwd`. Nothing downstream renames it — hook-command.ts:641-652 passes the payload through verbatim to stdin and NESSY_EVENT_DATA — so an imported Claude plugin hook reading `.old_cwd` or `.new_cwd` gets undefined. Fix is two keys at the emitter (emit `old_cwd`/`new_cwd` in addition to `cwd`) plus the type and the contract row. Separately out of scope for this row: hooks.md:2430/2451 also specify `CLAUDE_ENV_FILE` access and a `watchPaths` output for CwdChanged, and plans/2026-07-29-hook-context-injection.md:302 already records that our CwdChanged hooks' env writes are never read.
